evidence.excerpt: This paper describes an integrated pre-compliance workflow for mixed-signal PCB development that combines three techniques used sequentially across the design cycle. In the early layout phase, an automated rule-checking tool flags geometric violations associated with known emission risks. At the prototype stage, near-field scanning at 3 mm standoff generates spatial emission maps that identify dominant radiating structures. Finally, FDTD simulation using geometry extracted from the identified hotspots provides frequency-resolved quantification and supports what-if analysis of corrective measures. The workflow was applied to four prototype boards developed in collaboration with two regional electronics companies. Across all four boards, the integrated workflow identified the dominant emission source correctly in each case; corrective measures applied on the basis of simulation results reduced the peak radiated emission at the pre-compliance test receiver by between 5.2 dB and 11.7 dB before formal OATS measurement. Time-to-compliance for the four designs averaged 2.1 fewer test-and-rework cycles compared to a historical baseline of designs developed without structured pre-compliance analysis. The workflow documentation and rule-checker code are deposited in an open repository.
